about: What each fixture in wasm/ declares, how an inspector must judge it, and what a host must observe running it. Rejection codes are citadel-app-abi-inspect's Rejection::code(). A run's `report` is the fixture's `log` lines `<probe>=<answer>`; answers are ok | ungranted | unavailable:<r> | limit:<w> | policy:<r> | remote:<n> | code:<abi error>. Refusals answer at once; a host may make any other granted call except canvas and log pending, and the fixture then reports it when its reply_ready arrives, so compare reports after every pending reply has been delivered. The intrinsic capabilities (canvas, ui, events, navigate, log) are held by every install. `host` is the reference host's policy for the run; the TS host must be configured the same to compare.

hello-canvas.about: The control. Subscribes to pointer events, asks for frames, paints a card.

linker-start.about: hello-canvas linked with only --import-memory: wasm-ld adds a start function to zero .bss. Negative control for the fixtures' link flags.

undeclared-import.about: Imports net (a server fetch) while declaring no net.* capability.

foreign-import.about: Imports env.fetch, wasm-bindgen glue and a WASI function.

over-memory.about: Grows past the ceiling (2 GiB at once, then page by page), then allocates 64 MiB infallibly and dies.

ungranted-calls.about: Calls every group an install must be granted (all but the intrinsic ones), and an ungranted group raw with a bogus op, garbage and an out-of-bounds pointer. init answers 0 only if every answer was exactly {refused: "ungranted"} at once; 100 + group index of the first that was not; 200/201 for the raw probes.

panics.about: Panics in app_event on UiAction{id:"panic"}; handles every other event.

huge-reply.about: Asks for a 4 GiB read (host limit), an 8 MiB read its 4 MiB memory cannot hold (SDK limit, no trap), and 16 bytes (the control).

exfil-attempts.about: Granted only log, tries every way out through the SDK and at the raw boundary.

ihttp-stream-client.about: A client holding only ihttp.call streams a 10-chunk response, more than the initial credit of 4: chunks 5-10 come only because the SDK returns credit with IhttpConsumed, which either ihttp capability admits. A host that admits IhttpConsumed for ihttp.serve alone stalls it after 4 chunks and `stream` is never reported. host.ihttp_remote is the far end the host must play: status 200, `chunks` body frames of `chunk_bytes` bytes, sent under the caller's credit (4, plus one per IhttpConsumed), then End. The control run holds only ihttp.serve, which must not admit the call itself.
